title: 2008 AMC 10B Problem 10
statement: Points \(A\) and \(B\) are on a circle of radius \(5\) and \(AB=6.\) Point \(C\) is the midpoint of the minor arc \(AB.\) What is the length of the line segment \(AC?\)

solutions.text:
Let \(O\) be the center and \(D\) the midpoint of \(AB.\) Then \(OD\perp AB\) with \(AD=3,\) so \(OD=\sqrt{5^2-3^2}=4.\)

Since \(C\) is the midpoint of the minor arc, \(O,\) \(D,\) \(C\) are collinear and \(DC=OC-OD=5-4=1.\)

Then \(AC=\sqrt{AD^2+DC^2}\) \(=\sqrt{3^2+1^2}\) \(=\sqrt{10}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: The line from the center through \(C\) perpendicularly bisects chord \(AB\)
Find the center-to-chord distance, subtract from \(5\) to reach \(C,\) then use the right triangle with leg \(3\)
